stages.name: Independent peoples
stages.desc: Iberian, Celtiberian and Lusitanian peoples outside any empire

stages.name: Carthage's home government
stages.desc: Ruled from the city by its council and suffetes, with Hanno's African conquests

stages.name: Barcid command
stages.desc: Held by Hamilcar, Hasdrubal or Hannibal, with little oversight from home

stages.name: Rome
stages.desc: Rome, its Italian allies and its provinces

stages.name: Numidian kingdoms
stages.desc: The Massylian and Masaesylian kings of the interior

stages.name: War zone
stages.desc: Contested ground, in revolt or under invasion

states.name: Spain
timeline: Iberian and Celtiberian peoples; Gades and a few Phoenician ports trade with Carthage
Hamilcar lands at Gades and conquers the south, answering to almost no one at home
Hamilcar drowns; his son-in-law Hasdrubal takes command, chosen by the army
Hasdrubal agrees with Rome not to cross the Ebro in arms
Hasdrubal is murdered; the army acclaims Hannibal, aged about twenty-six
Hannibal besieges Saguntum, Rome's friend, for eight months
Gnaeus Scipio lands at Emporion; Spain becomes a second front
Publius Scipio takes New Carthage in a single day
Victory at Ilipa; Gades goes over to Rome and the Carthaginians leave Spain
Rome organises two provinces, Nearer and Further Spain

states.name: Libya
timeline: The Emporia: Lepcis, Oea and Sabratha pay rich tribute to Carthage
Still Carthaginian, but Masinissa now eyes the Emporia

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage and its Libyan farmland; Hanno the Great campaigns inland and taxes the countryside hard
Peace with Rome; twenty thousand unpaid mercenaries come home from Sicily
The Truceless War: mercenaries and Libyan towns rise; Utica and Hippo are besieged
Hamilcar and Hanno, reconciled, crush the last rebels; Hanno keeps his grip on Africa
After Cannae, Hanno asks the council what Hannibal's victories have really won
Scipio lands near Utica; the Great Plains are lost in 203
Hannibal, recalled from Italy, is defeated at Zama
Peace: Carthage keeps its African core but owes ten thousand talents and may not wage war without Rome
Hannibal as suffete limits the judges to one-year terms and reforms the treasury
Denounced to Rome by his enemies, Hannibal flees by night to the East

states.name: Italy
timeline: Rome and its Italian allies; in western Sicily, Hamilcar holds out at Heircte
Rome wins at the Aegates Islands; Carthage gives up Sicily
Rome seizes Sardinia while Carthage is still fighting its mercenaries
Hannibal crosses the Alps and wins at the Trebia
Cannae: southern Italian cities go over to Hannibal
Capua falls back to Rome; Syracuse fell the year before
Hannibal sails home from Croton; Italy is Rome's again

states.name: Algeria
timeline: Massylian kings in the east, Masaesylian in the west; Hanno's campaigns reach Theveste on the frontier
The Numidian prince Naravas brings two thousand horsemen over to Hamilcar
Syphax of the Masaesyli treats with Rome and fights Carthage
Masinissa, after serving Carthage in Spain, changes sides
Syphax is captured; Masinissa takes his kingdom
Masinissa reigns over all Numidia as Rome's ally on Carthage's border

states.name: Portugal
timeline: Lusitanian and Celtic peoples of the Atlantic west
Lusitanian warriors serve as mercenaries, but the west stays independent
Lusitanians raid Roman Further Spain

events.title: Hamilcar at Heircte
events.text: Hamilcar Barca takes the Sicilian command and fortifies Mount Heircte above Panormus.

events.title: Hannibal is born
events.text: Hamilcar's first son, Hannibal, is born at Carthage around this year.

events.title: Hanno's African wars
events.text: Hanno the Great campaigns inland and takes Hecatompylos, probably Theveste.

events.title: Hamilcar at Eryx
events.text: Hamilcar seizes the town of Eryx and holds out against Roman siege lines.

events.title: Aegates Islands
events.text: A Roman fleet destroys Carthage's relief convoy; Carthage sues for peace.

events.title: Peace of Lutatius
events.text: Carthage gives up Sicily and pays an indemnity; Hamilcar hands over and goes home.

events.title: Mercenaries at Sicca
events.text: The returning mercenaries wait at Sicca for pay that Hanno cannot or will not give.

events.title: Revolt at Tunis
events.text: Led by Spendius and Matho, the mercenaries and Libyan towns take up arms.

events.title: Hanno fails at Utica
events.text: Hanno's elephants break the rebel camp, but his army is surprised and routed.

events.title: Battle of the Bagradas
events.text: Hamilcar crosses the river mouth by night and defeats the rebels.

events.title: The generals quarrel
events.text: Hamilcar and Hanno cannot work together; the army is asked to choose, and Hanno is dismissed.

events.title: Battle of the Saw
events.text: Hamilcar traps the rebel army in a defile and destroys it.

events.title: Matho defeated
events.text: Hamilcar and Hanno, reconciled, defeat Matho near Leptis Minor.

events.title: Rome takes Sardinia
events.text: Rome seizes Sardinia and adds to the indemnity; Carthage cannot resist.

events.title: Hamilcar to Spain
events.text: Hamilcar lands at Gades with young Hannibal, sworn never to be a friend of Rome.

events.title: Rome asks questions
events.text: A Roman embassy asks Hamilcar why he is in Spain; to pay Rome, he says.

events.title: Hamilcar drowns
events.text: Hamilcar dies in a river while retreating from the siege of Helice.

events.title: New Carthage
events.text: Hasdrubal founds Qart Hadasht on a superb harbour, a capital of his own.

events.title: Ebro agreement
events.text: Hasdrubal agrees with Rome not to cross the Ebro in arms.

events.title: Hannibal acclaimed
events.text: Hasdrubal is murdered; the army chooses Hannibal and Carthage confirms him.

events.title: Siege of Saguntum
events.text: Hannibal besieges Rome's friend Saguntum; Hanno urges the council to hand him over.

events.title: War is declared
events.text: Roman envoys at Carthage offer peace or war; the council accepts war.

events.title: Scipio at Emporion
events.text: Gnaeus Scipio lands in north-east Spain and opens a second front.

events.title: The Trebia
events.text: Fresh from the Alps, Hannibal destroys a consular army in the snow.

events.title: Lake Trasimene
events.text: Hannibal ambushes a Roman army on the lakeshore.

events.title: Cannae
events.text: Hannibal encircles and destroys the largest army Rome had ever fielded.

events.title: Gold rings
events.text: Mago pours Roman gold rings before the council; Hanno asks for peace.

events.title: Reinforcements to Spain
events.text: Carthage sends Mago's army to Spain rather than Italy.

events.title: Syphax turns
events.text: The Numidian king Syphax makes terms with Rome against Carthage.

events.title: Tarentum taken
events.text: Hannibal captures Tarentum, though its citadel holds out.

events.title: Capua falls
events.text: Rome retakes Capua; Hannibal's march on Rome fails to save it.

events.title: New Carthage falls
events.text: Publius Cornelius Scipio storms the Barcid capital in Spain.

events.title: The Metaurus
events.text: Hasdrubal Barca, bringing an army from Spain, is killed in Italy.

events.title: Ilipa
events.text: Scipio defeats the last Carthaginian field army in Spain.

events.title: Gades surrenders
events.text: The old Phoenician city goes over to Rome.

events.title: Scipio in Africa
events.text: Scipio lands near Utica and besieges it.

events.title: Syphax captured
events.text: Masinissa and Laelius defeat and capture Syphax; Cirta opens its gates.

events.title: Hannibal recalled
events.text: Hannibal leaves Italy from Croton after fifteen years.

events.title: Zama
events.text: Scipio and Masinissa defeat Hannibal; Hannibal urges acceptance of peace.

events.title: Peace with Rome
events.text: Carthage surrenders its fleet and owes ten thousand talents over fifty years.

events.title: Two Spanish provinces
events.text: Rome creates Nearer and Further Spain.

events.title: Hannibal as suffete
events.text: Elected chief magistrate, Hannibal ends life terms for the judges and pursues embezzlers.

events.title: Flight by night
events.text: Warned of a Roman embassy, Hannibal rides to his coastal estate and sails for Tyre.

chartNote: Share of the area of six present-day countries (Spain, Portugal, Italy, Tunisia, Algeria and Libya), by who controlled most of each. Regions are today's boundaries, so Sicily and Sardinia count with Italy and the desert inflates Libya and Algeria; the map is a simplification. Its categories follow largely Roman sources, which cast Carthage's politics as a feud between a 'peace party' and a 'war party': a picture historians still debate.
